public.title: Deep Merge
public.description: input {left,right}; recursively merge object pairs, retaining left-only keys and taking right values otherwise. Arrays are replaced whole, never concatenated; null is a value. Return the merged JSON value. Neither input is modified. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, fixtures and reference solutions, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party exercise text or implementation copied.

explanation: Recurse only when both values are ordinary objects; all other conflicts choose a deep copy of right. Worst-case O(n times h) time from repeated copying, O(n plus h) space. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
